official.deadline_note: 15 January 2027 is the main-round application deadline for autumn 2027 entry and the latest date to hold a Umeå University programme as priority 1 on University Admissions - the gate for scholarship eligibility. Scholarship-specific dates for the 2027 cycle are not yet published. In the last published (2026) cycle the sequence was: application fee paid by 2 February, personal invitation emails 4-9 February, interest-registration deadline 4 March (23:59 CET), and results announced by email 17 April. The university notes the dates are preliminary and subject to change.
official.application_cycle: Autumn 2027 entry, main (first) admissions round - application opens 16 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027, autumn semester starts 30 August 2027. The 2026 scholarship cycle has concluded (results announced 17 April 2026); the university still publishes the 2026 timeline.
official.status_note: The official Scholarships page is live and recruiting for the next cycle. The most recent published scholarship timeline covers the 2026 cycle (priority 1 by 15 January 2026, application fee by 2 February 2026, invitations 4-9 February 2026, interest deadline 4 March 2026, results 17 April 2026), and the next round runs alongside autumn 2027 admission, whose main application round opens 16 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027. The 2027 scholarship timeline has not yet been published.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: "Umeå University offers scholarships each autumn semester, in conjunction with the autumn semester admission, to academically talented and high-achieving students. Scholarships are offered in the form of tuition-waivers. Selected candidates receive a full or partial waiver of the tuition fee." The FAQ adds: "In general, the scholarship covers full or part of the tuition fee."
benefits: A full or partial waiver of the tuition fee for the programme, awarded in the form of a tuition waiver
eligibility: Are a citizen of a country outside of the EU/EEA and Switzerland
Have applied for a full programme at Umeå University (Bachelor's or Master's) in the first (international) admissions round
Have completed the application for programme studies before the application deadline on 15 January
Have paid the application fee by 2 February (students exempt from the application fee but required to pay tuition fees are also considered eligible)
Have chosen a Umeå University programme as priority 1 on the University Admissions website by 15 January at the latest

Current students: have paid the tuition fee for the Spring semester and be a registered student on that semester; students on study leave are not eligible, as are applicants to the double degree Master's Programme in Sustainability Reporting and Financial Analysis
requirements: The programme application must be completed at University Admissions before the 15 January deadline and the application fee paid by the published February deadline; the application is not processed until the fee is paid or fee-exempt status is proved
Demonstrate proficiency in English by means of an internationally recognised test such as TOEFL, IELTS or the equivalent, or through previous upper-secondary or university studies

Bachelor's applicants: an upper-secondary/high school education that makes them eligible for higher education studies in their home country, plus a mathematics requirement for students who received final school grades after 31 December 2009

Master's applicants: a Bachelor's degree from an internationally recognised university (minimum three years / 180 ECTS, with at least 60 ECTS in one discipline); results below second class are not accepted and study results under 50% will not be considered
Register interest only through the personal invitation email sent in early February to the email address registered on the University Admissions account
documents: Supporting documents uploaded to the University Admissions account demonstrating previous studies and English proficiency
Documentation of citizenship / fee status as required by University Admissions' country-specific instructions
Country-specific application documents - some countries require hardcopy submission or verification, per the country instructions for Bachelor's or Master's studies
Additional portfolio documents for architecture, design and fine arts programmes, submitted per the instructions on the specific programme page
Final-year Bachelor's applicants must upload the complete transcript and degree certificate before the programme starts in order to register as programme students
selection_criteria: After the deadline to register interest has passed, a committee within each respective faculty selects candidates
Selections are based on the applicant's academic merit, as well as any other relevant information shared in the registration form

Only applicants with a Umeå University programme as priority 1 on University Admissions as of their application deadline, or second-year Master's students currently in their first year, are eligible to register interest
coverage: Full or partial waiver of the tuition fee for the programme (a tuition waiver, not a cash payment)
Degree-programme tuition fees at Umeå University range from SEK 96,600 to SEK 395,700 per year depending on the field of study - the waiver removes or reduces this invoice
application_method: Apply for a full Bachelor's or Master's programme at universityadmissions.se in the main (first) admissions round and rank the Umeå University programme as priority 1 by 15 January
Pay the SEK 900 application fee by the published February deadline (or document fee-exempt status)
Watch for the personal invitation email sent 4-9 February to the address registered on University Admissions, checking the spam folder if it does not arrive
Register interest for a scholarship using the link in that email before the early-March deadline (4 March, 23:59 CET, in the 2026 cycle)
Await the result, announced by email on the published announcement date (17 April in the 2026 cycle)
official.application_route: Apply and rank priority 1 through the national portal universityadmissions.se, pay the application fee, then register interest via the personal invitation emailed in early February - there is no separate scholarship application form.
official.study_mode: Full-time (30 credits per semester; scholarship eligibility requires having applied for a full programme)
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a country outside of the EU/EEA and Switzerland; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens are not required to pay tuition fees and fall outside this scheme
official.international_eligibility: Yes - by design the scholarship is only for citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland, i.e. fee-paying international students on English-language degree programmes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to any full English-language degree programme at Umeå University, except the Master's Programme in Sustainability Reporting and Financial Analysis, which is a double degree programme and not eligible
official.duration: Awarded each autumn semester in conjunction with the autumn semester admission; selected candidates receive a full or partial waiver of the tuition fee for their programme
official.description: Umeå University offers scholarships each autumn semester, in conjunction with the autumn semester admission, to academically talented and high-achieving students from outside the EU/EEA. Scholarships are offered in the form of tuition-waivers, and selected candidates receive a full or partial waiver of the tuition fee. The university states it does not offer any other forms of financial support and recommends applicants look for external funding if needed.
official.program_type: University-administered tuition-fee waiver for international (non-EU/EEA) Bachelor's and Master's students
official.english_requirement: For most Master's level programmes the requirement is the equivalent of the Swedish upper-secondary course English 6: IELTS 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL 90, by an internationally recognised test; the requirement can also be met through previous upper-secondary studies or previous university studies in certain countries, and some programmes have a higher requirement

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period - the award is published only as a full or partial tuition-fee waiver, so no fixed monetary figure exists on any umu.se page; the SEK 96,600-395,700 range is the tuition fee level, not the scholarship value
The 2027 cycle scholarship dates (invitation window, interest-registration deadline, results date) - only the 2026 cycle timeline is published
Whether a waiver continues into later study years or applies per academic year
How recipients are split between full and partial waivers, and whether the share is chosen by the applicant or decided by the faculty committee
The number of scholarships awarded per cycle

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition waiver, not a cash award: you apply normally through universityadmissions.se, rank a Umeå programme first, and the university emails eligible non-EU/EEA applicants a personal invitation in early February with the link to register interest. Faculty committees then select on academic merit and the decision arrives by email in mid-April. Budget separately for living costs, housing, travel and the residence permit - the university explicitly states it offers no other financial support. Treat your priority 1 choice as the real commitment, because the scholarship is tied to that programme and cannot be moved to another Umeå programme afterwards.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically strong non-EU/EEA applicants who can win a fee-liable Umeå bachelor's or master's place, need tuition relief, and can still self-fund living costs and migration expenses.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply at universityadmissions.se in the main round (opens 16 October 2026, closes 15 January 2027) and set the Umeå programme as priority 1 - not priority 2-4 - before the deadline
Pay the SEK 900 application fee by the February deadline, or document fee-exempt status if you are exempt but still tuition-liable
Upload country-correct documents (transcripts, degree certificate, English test or prior-study proof) by the supporting-documents deadline of 1 February 2027
Keep the email address on your University Admissions account active and monitored, including the spam folder, from early February - registration is only possible through the emailed invitation link

Complete the interest-registration form fully before the early-March deadline, writing up your academic record in detail since faculty committees score merit plus other relevant information in the form
Line up funding for living costs and, in case of a partial waiver, the remaining tuition (SEK 96,600-395,700 per year depending on the programme)
common_rejection_risks: Ranking another university or another Umeå programme as priority 1 - the scholarship follows the priority 1 programme and is lost with it
Missing the roughly four-week interest window between the early-February invitation and the early-March deadline because the email went to an unmonitored address or spam folder
Paying the application fee late - the application is not processed at all without it
Applying to the Master's Programme in Sustainability Reporting and Financial Analysis, a double degree that is explicitly not eligible
Assuming the award can be transferred after being admitted to a different Umeå programme - the university states this is not possible
Late or wrongly formatted document uploads (country-specific rules) that delay the admission decision past the semester start date
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, housing, travel, residence-permit and insurance expenses are not covered, and a partial waiver leaves the remaining tuition of SEK 96,600-395,700 per year (depending on programme) to be self-funded; umu.se states it offers no other forms of financial support.
document_audit: Follow your country's document rules exactly - some countries require hardcopy submission or institutional verification, which takes weeks to arrange

English proof: IELTS 6.5 with no band below 5.5 or TOEFL 90 is the English 6 baseline for most master's programmes; some programmes demand a higher level, and master's results below second class or under 50% are not accepted
Citizenship must be documented at University Admissions to establish fee status - the same documentation establishes scholarship eligibility, so errors here are doubly costly
Design, architecture and fine arts applicants face separate portfolio submission instructions on the programme page
Final-year bachelor's applicants must upload the complete transcript and degree certificate before the programme start or they cannot register as programme students
alerts: The university labels the scholarship dates preliminary and subject to change - re-check the umu.se Scholarships page and your University Admissions account from January onwards

Scholarships cannot be deferred; if you decline the year, email tuitionfees@umu.se to withdraw so the award can pass to another applicant, and note that studies can simply be re-applied for in a later round

Non-EU/EEA applicants must use the first (main) admissions round - the second round leaves too little time for a residence permit, and no residence permit is issued for less than full-time (30 credits per semester) study

Tuition invoices are issued in SEK with a hard payment deadline (10 May for the autumn semester) and any shortfall from conversion or intermediary bank fees is the student's responsibility; late payment means losing the programme place
Current students must have paid the spring tuition fee and be registered for spring - study leave disqualifies you entirely
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply and rank priority 1 at universityadmissions.se by 15 January, pay the application fee, then wait for the emailed invitation (early February) whose link opens the interest-registration form that closes in early March; the outcome arrives by email in April.
